X.note: The terrain relief map is decent but flat and has no country or region context. The callout box sits below the pin and covers the coast. The Ulsan marker is a tiny box plus a separate orange dot, so it's unclear which one marks the city. The callout gives a single 1962 number with nothing to compare it to, and no route or movement is shown. The caption ('the yard's customers were abroad') has no visual link to the map. The source line is small and low-contrast, and the caption sits in a dark gradient that hides map detail.

Y.note: The globe render is rich, with atmosphere glow and Texas highlighted in orange, so the place reads at once. The callout is large and high-contrast, with a clear title and rule line. The 'As of' date chip adds honesty. Weak points: the callout is wide and covers part of the Gulf and the southern US, and the source line is small and dim. The caption and callout say slightly different things. No route or movement is shown, only a highlighted state.

why: Y puts a clearly highlighted region on a recognizable globe with a large, legible callout and a date stamp, while X has a vague tiny marker, no geographic anchor and a caption disconnected from the map.
top_fix_for_weaker: Zoom out so Korea and Japan show with labels, or add an inset locator. Replace the tiny box and dot with one large pulsing Ulsan marker with a leader line to the callout. Move the callout off the coast. Show the claimed route or flow, such as arrows to customer countries, so the caption's 'customers abroad' is visible. Brighten and enlarge the source line.
